title: Lancaster Street West expropriation authorization advances
subtitle: Drinking water report, Westmount Road design, Scheifele Bridge lands, Charles Street turn limits and transit ridership.
overview: The committee recommended that Council authorize the first step toward expropriating small strips of land for Phase 1 of the Lancaster Street West improvements in Kitchener {{vote:m8}}. A motion to send the report back to staff for a project timeline was defeated {{vote:m7}}. Staff said negotiations with owners continue and the process would stop for any property acquired by agreement.

The committee also endorsed the 2024 Drinking Water Summary Report {{vote:m6}}, which included a title change for the system owner's representative. Staff reported strong inspection results and outlined work on water supply, asset management and conservation, including a greywater pilot.

Through the consent agenda {{vote:m1}}, the committee recommended approving the Westmount Road design in Kitchener, endorsing updated water operational plans, approving expropriation for the Scheifele Bridge replacement in Woolwich, and adding turn restrictions on Charles Street at Cedar Street. These are recommendations for Council to consider.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended authorizing the Regional Solicitor to start the application process to expropriate partial strips and temporary easements for Lancaster Street West between Bridgeport Road East and Elizabeth Street.
A motion to refer the Lancaster Street West report back to staff with a project phase timeline was defeated.

The committee recommended endorsing the report, the management review, the infrastructure maintenance plan update, and renaming the system owner's representative title to Director, Water and Wastewater Operations.
The committee recommended approving the preferred design for Westmount Road between Fischer-Hallman Road and Block Line Road in Kitchener.
The committee recommended approving expropriation of a partial taking and temporary easements for replacing the Scheifele Bridge on Northfield Drive East in Woolwich.
The committee recommended by-law amendments to prohibit southbound U-turns and certain right and left turns (bicycles excepted) at Charles Street and Cedar Street in Kitchener.
The committee recommended endorsing updated operational plans for the new Petersburg system and the modified St. Clements-Heidelberg system.

debate: One councillor questioned starting expropriation while negotiations continue, saying it is a strong tool to use only when necessary, and noted most construction funding falls in later years.

Staff said this is the standard first report, negotiations began last summer and continue, and the process takes about 9 to 12 months, or around 18 months with negotiation. They said starting now helps secure land and utility relocation before construction.

Another councillor asked whether the wording could feel like a threat to owners, referring to earlier community concerns elsewhere. Staff said the report only begins an application and ends for any owner who reaches agreement.

Supporters said the parcels are small slivers of land and the process is the fastest and simplest. One councillor said a referral would not yield information not already available. The referring councillor said the motion was premature without more justification.

During the transit item, a councillor asked whether online booking affects undelivered-trip counts for Mobility Plus. Staff said sessions are counted the same way for online and phone and that replacement software should capture this better.

On drinking water, councillors asked about tariff effects on valves and parts, growth and climate pressures, and greywater. Staff said the asset management plan will set priorities and that conservation and local groundwater are being explored.
